From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@integrix.com>

Subject: RE: Integrix kickoff — technical notes (SDK, routing, embeddings)

Putting together some technical notes to unblock the deep-dive: 

1) SDK quickstart repo + samples (public): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart — contains python/ts examples and a local sandbox runner that emulates the hosted API.

2) Auth patterns:
  - API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY and run the quickstart. Good for rapid POC.
  - OIDC: we support standard OIDC flows; for the lab we can provide a dev client and a one-click callback URL; for dedicated/private we'll map your IdP metadata.

3) Routing & environments:
  - Local dev routes to redwood sandbox (no billing) via REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox;
  - Hosted (redwood API) vs Dedicated: demonstrate routing via the SDK config: {"routePolicy": "latency-first"} or pinned to model variant. (We'll enumerate exact flags in the runbook.)

4) Structured output / tool-calling:
  - Example uses function spec + JSONSchema validate step in the SDK sample. We will include both a synchronous tool-call stub (local HTTP webhook) and an async example that writes to a mocked queue.

5) Embeddings & reranker:
  - Endpoint: /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank; sample pipeline in samples/emb_rerank.py and ts/samples/emb-rerank.ts.
  - We need expected average doc length and target QPS to recommend quantization/batch sizes — Anika, can you confirm average doc size (tokens) and whether you expect bursty search or steady QPS?

I've zipped a minimal set of starter templates (rdw-sdk-templates.zip) that we'll attach to the demo email.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Architect, Platform Integrations

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@integrix.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-20T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integrix SDK lab prep — local runbook + quick commands

Thanks team — looping up the lab runbook items so Integrix can try them before the Wed deep-dive. Short quickstart steps below (copied from the repo with minimal edits):

Python (local sandbox):
  1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart
  2) cd sdk-quickstart/python && python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  3) pip install -r requirements.txt
  4) export REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox
  5) export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<paste-temporary-key>" (or configure OIDC later)
  6) python examples/structured_output_demo.py --dataset ../sample-corpus.csv

Expected output: a JSONL file in /tmp/rdw_out with two tool calls resolved (webhook stub) and a rerank score column appended.

TypeScript (local dev):
  1) cd sdk-quickstart/ts && npm install
  2) export REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox && export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<paste-temporary-key>"
  3) npm run start:structured -- --input ../sample-corpus.csv

Local sandbox notes: the sandbox mimics the hosted API but limits seq length to 1024 tokens and QPS to 20 for the POC. For any higher QPS during the lab we can temporarily lift throttles if you notify us in advance.

Deep-dive agenda (Wed 5/22 09:00 PT):
  - 09:00-09:15: overview & auth (Irene)
  - 09:15-09:35: SDK quickstart walkthrough (Karthik)
  - 09:35-09:50: embeddings/rerank target metrics (Integrix)
  - 09:50-10:00: next steps, procurement ask items (Prio)

I'll upload the explicit runbook to the Integrix project in Console and share the link before the meeting. Anything to add before I publish?

- Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Auth: we'll plan to use API key for the POC but will validate OIDC in the deep-dive.
- Procurement: procurement@integrix.com confirms they received the MAP and will follow up with SOW/PO items in the week after.
